ai.definition: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) are nuclear reactors with an output of less than 300 megawatts that can be mass-produced in factories and deployed flexibly at various locations.
ai.howItWorks: SMRs use standardized modular components manufactured in a factory setting, which are then transported to the site for assembly. They employ passive cooling systems and compact reactor cores designed to enhance safety and reduce operational complexity.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the high costs and construction risks associated with traditional large-scale nuclear reactors by leveraging economies of scale through mass production and reducing on-site construction time.
ai.manufacturing: SMRs are produced in standardized modules, allowing for efficient manufacturing processes and reduced variability compared to custom-built reactors.
ai.buildProcess: Modules are fabricated off-site, then transported to the site where they are assembled. This modular approach minimizes on-site labor and reduces the risk of construction delays.
ai.costDrivers: Initial capital investment in factory production lines, transportation costs for modules, and regulatory compliance requirements.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to see increased deployment as regulations are clarified and economies of scale become more apparent.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks vary by country; ongoing efforts focus on developing standardized safety guidelines and licensing processes for SMRs.
ai.risks: Technological, operational, financial, and regulatory risks associated with new technologies. Safety concerns remain a significant barrier to widespread adoption.
ai.profitability: Potential for cost savings in the long term due to reduced construction costs and increased efficiency; however, initial investment and regulatory hurdles may limit near-term profitability.
ai.futureDevelopment: Ongoing research focuses on improving safety features, enhancing passive cooling systems, and developing advanced reactor designs. Collaboration between industry and government is expected to drive further advancements.

glossary.def: Describing a system or component that can be produced in standardized units for easy assembly.
A safety feature where the reactor's cooling systems rely on natural processes (e.g., gravity, convection) rather than mechanical pumps and external power sources.

subsystems.name: Reactor core and fuel
subsystems.role: sustains a controlled fission chain reaction.
parts: low-enriched uranium fuel assemblies (some advanced designs need HALEU)

subsystems.name: Integral reactor module
subsystems.role: in many designs the pressure vessel also contains the steam generators and pressuriser, removing large external pipes.

subsystems.name: Passive safety systems
subsystems.role: cool the core by natural circulation and gravity, with no pumps or power needed for days.

subsystems.name: Power conversion
subsystems.role: turns reactor heat into electricity or industrial heat.

subsystems.name: Containment and siting
subsystems.role: contains any release; often placed below ground.

buildSteps.title: Certify the design
buildSteps.detail: The standardised design goes through years of regulator review — done once, then reused for every unit.

buildSteps.title: Build modules in a factory
buildSteps.detail: Pressure vessel, steam generators and internals are forged, welded and inspected in a factory, then shipped by road, rail or barge.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: Site licensing, excavation and construction of the reactor building and turbine hall.

buildSteps.title: Make the fuel
buildSteps.detail: Uranium is enriched, pressed into ceramic pellets, sealed in rods and bundled into assemblies.

buildSteps.title: Install and connect
buildSteps.detail: Modules are lifted into place and connected to the turbine hall and the grid.

buildSteps.title: Start up
buildSteps.detail: Fuel is loaded, low-power physics tests confirm the core behaves as designed, and power is raised step by step to full operation.

prerequisites.why: most SMRs are scaled-down versions of proven reactor types.

prerequisites.tech: Factory fabrication of nuclear components at volume
prerequisites.why: the whole cost case depends on factory production lines that are not yet running.
several advanced designs need higher-enriched fuel with very little production capacity outside Russia.
savings only come if unit two is not reviewed from scratch.
first-of-a-kind projects have overrun budgets; the claimed savings are unproven.

pathway.milestone: a few units operate in Russia and China
pathway.unlocks: proof the designs run; their costs are not transparent.

pathway.milestone: first Western units under construction (e.g. the BWRX-300 at Darlington, Canada)

pathway.unlocks: factory learning — cost only falls if the same design is built many times.

pathway.milestone: advanced non-water SMRs (molten salt, high-temperature gas)
pathway.unlocks: high-temperature heat for industry, not just electricity.
